lessons.title: Test an even function
lessons.objective: Explain the method, justify each calculation step, and check the result: test an even function.

blocks.text: Foundations and symbols
A function assigns an output to an input. An even function gives the same output when the input changes sign, throughout a domain symmetric about zero.
Understand the concept
Substitute the entire negative input inside brackets; checking one input pair alone does not prove the identity.
Worked example

steps.explanation: Replace every occurrence of x with the whole expression minus x.
Squaring multiplies the expression by itself. Two negative factors give a positive product.
The output is unchanged for every real input, so the function is even.

check.explanation: This pair illustrates the symbolic proof; it is not a substitute for that proof.

blocks.text: Guided practice
Before calculating, identify the rule and any domain restrictions. Follow the same steps as the example, and explain why each operation is valid.

blocks.question: Which relation defines an even function?
options: f(x) is never defined at zero
blocks.explanation:
\[f(-x)=(-x)^2\]
Replace every occurrence of x with the whole expression minus x.

\[(-x)^2=(-x)(-x)=x^2\]
Squaring multiplies the expression by itself. Two negative factors give a positive product.

\[f(-x)=x^2=f(x)\]
The output is unchanged for every real input, so the function is even.

\[f(-3)=9=f(3)\]
This pair illustrates the symbolic proof; it is not a substitute for that proof.

blocks.text: Independent practice
Test whether \(g(x)=x^2+2\) is even. Write the intermediate calculations on separate lines, explain your choices, and check your answer before reading the answer below.

blocks.title: How to check your work
blocks.text: Compare the result with the original question. For an antiderivative, differentiate it; for an equation, substitute it back. Check signs, brackets, domains, and any constants.
Recap
Substitute the entire negative input inside brackets; checking one input pair alone does not prove the identity.

blocks.title: Avoid this mistake
blocks.text: An even function is not defined by producing even integers.

lessons.title: Test an odd function
lessons.objective: Explain the method, justify each calculation step, and check the result: test an odd function.

blocks.text: Foundations and symbols
An odd function changes the sign of its output when its input changes sign. This identity must hold throughout a domain symmetric about zero.
Understand the concept
Keep the negative input in brackets before applying the exponent.
Worked example

steps.explanation: Substitute minus x for the input, keeping its sign inside the power.
Two negative factors first give a positive product; multiplying by the third gives a negative product.
The output has the opposite sign of the original output for every real x.

check.explanation: The numerical check agrees with the identity.

blocks.text: Guided practice
Before calculating, identify the rule and any domain restrictions. Follow the same steps as the example, and explain why each operation is valid.

blocks.question: Which relation defines an odd function?
options: f(x) must be constant and nonzero
blocks.explanation:
\[f(-x)=(-x)^3\]
Substitute minus x for the input, keeping its sign inside the power.

\[(-x)^3=(-x)(-x)(-x)=-x^3\]
Two negative factors first give a positive product; multiplying by the third gives a negative product.

\[f(-x)=-x^3=-f(x)\]
The output has the opposite sign of the original output for every real x.

\[f(-2)=-8=-f(2)\]
The numerical check agrees with the identity.

blocks.text: Independent practice
Test whether \(g(x)=3x\) is odd. Write the intermediate calculations on separate lines, explain your choices, and check your answer before reading the answer below.

blocks.title: How to check your work
blocks.text: Compare the result with the original question. For an antiderivative, differentiate it; for an equation, substitute it back. Check signs, brackets, domains, and any constants.
Recap
Keep the negative input in brackets before applying the exponent.

blocks.title: Avoid this mistake
blocks.text: An odd function is not defined by producing odd integers.

lessons.title: Evaluate a polynomial limit
lessons.objective: Explain the method, justify each calculation step, and check the result: evaluate a polynomial limit.

blocks.text: Foundations and symbols
A limit describes the output approached as the input approaches a point. A polynomial is continuous, so its limit at a real point equals its value there.
Understand the concept
Establish that substitution is valid before substituting.
Worked example

steps.explanation: This is a polynomial, so continuity allows us to replace x by three.

check.explanation: Inputs just below and above three give outputs close to seven.

blocks.text: Guided practice
Before calculating, identify the rule and any domain restrictions. Follow the same steps as the example, and explain why each operation is valid.

blocks.question: What is the limit of 2x + 1 as x approaches 3?
blocks.explanation:
\[\lim_{x\to3}(2x+1)=2(3)+1\]
This is a polynomial, so continuity allows us to replace x by three.

\[2(3)+1=6+1\]
Carry out the multiplication first.

\[6+1=7\]
Add the remaining terms.

\[f(2.99)=6.98,\qquad f(3.01)=7.02\]
Inputs just below and above three give outputs close to seven.

blocks.text: Independent practice
Find \(\lim_{x\to2}(2x+1)\). Write the intermediate calculations on separate lines, explain your choices, and check your answer before reading the answer below.

blocks.title: How to check your work
blocks.text: Compare the result with the original question. For an antiderivative, differentiate it; for an equation, substitute it back. Check signs, brackets, domains, and any constants.
Recap
Establish that substitution is valid before substituting.

blocks.title: Avoid this mistake
blocks.text: Do not assume direct substitution resolves every limit without considering the expression.

lessons.title: Differentiate a power
lessons.objective: Explain the method, justify each calculation step, and check the result: differentiate a power.

blocks.text: Foundations and symbols
A derivative measures local rate of change. In the power rule, multiply by the old exponent and then reduce that exponent by one.
Understand the concept
The notation \(f\prime(x)\) means the derivative of f; the exponent on x is not the coefficient in front of it.
Worked example

steps.explanation: Use the power rule for this polynomial power; n denotes its exponent.
Here n is two. Multiply by two and subtract one from the exponent.
An exponent of one leaves x unchanged.

check.explanation: For nonzero h the difference quotient simplifies to two x plus h; letting h approach zero confirms the rule.

blocks.text: Guided practice
Before calculating, identify the rule and any domain restrictions. Follow the same steps as the example, and explain why each operation is valid.

blocks.question: What is the derivative of x squared?
blocks.explanation:
\[\frac{d}{dx}x^n=nx^{n-1}\]
Use the power rule for this polynomial power; n denotes its exponent.

\[f\prime(x)=2x^{2-1}\]
Here n is two. Multiply by two and subtract one from the exponent.

\[f\prime(x)=2x^1=2x\]
An exponent of one leaves x unchanged.

\[\frac{(x+h)^2-x^2}{h}=2x+h\ \longrightarrow\ 2x\]
For nonzero h the difference quotient simplifies to two x plus h; letting h approach zero confirms the rule.

blocks.text: Independent practice
Differentiate \(x^3\). Write the intermediate calculations on separate lines, explain your choices, and check your answer before reading the answer below.

blocks.title: How to check your work
blocks.text: Compare the result with the original question. For an antiderivative, differentiate it; for an equation, substitute it back. Check signs, brackets, domains, and any constants.
Recap
The notation \(f\prime(x)\) means the derivative of f; the exponent on x is not the coefficient in front of it.

blocks.title: Avoid this mistake
blocks.text: The derivative of x² is not x or 2 alone; both coefficient and remaining power matter.

lessons.title: Explain the constant rule
lessons.objective: Explain the method, justify each calculation step, and check the result: explain the constant rule.

blocks.text: Foundations and symbols
A constant function has the same output at every input. Its output change is zero even when the input changes.
Understand the concept
A derivative divides output change by input change, then takes a limit as the input change approaches zero.
Worked example

steps.explanation: Both outputs equal seven, so their difference is zero.
For any nonzero input change, dividing the zero output change gives zero.
The quotient stays zero as the input change approaches zero.

check.explanation: Different inputs produce no output change, agreeing with zero slope.

blocks.text: Guided practice
Before calculating, identify the rule and any domain restrictions. Follow the same steps as the example, and explain why each operation is valid.

blocks.question: What is the derivative of the constant 7?
blocks.explanation:
\[f(x+h)-f(x)=7-7=0\]
Both outputs equal seven, so their difference is zero.

\[\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=\frac0h=0\quad(h\ne0)\]
For any nonzero input change, dividing the zero output change gives zero.

\[f\prime(x)=\lim_{h\to0}0=0\]
The quotient stays zero as the input change approaches zero.

\[f(2)=7,\qquad f(5)=7\]
Different inputs produce no output change, agreeing with zero slope.

blocks.text: Independent practice
Differentiate the constant function \(g(x)=-4\). Write the intermediate calculations on separate lines, explain your choices, and check your answer before reading the answer below.

blocks.title: How to check your work
blocks.text: Compare the result with the original question. For an antiderivative, differentiate it; for an equation, substitute it back. Check signs, brackets, domains, and any constants.

blocks.title: Independent practice answer
blocks.text: \[g\prime(x)=0\]
Recap
A derivative divides output change by input change, then takes a limit as the input change approaches zero.

blocks.title: Avoid this mistake
blocks.text: A constant's derivative is zero, not the original constant.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = x + 2, what is f(3)?
questions.explanation:
\[f(3)=3+2\]
Replace the input x by three in the given function.

\[3+2=5\]
Add to obtain the output.

\[f(-x)=(-x)^2\]
Replace every occurrence of x with the whole expression minus x.

\[(-x)^2=(-x)(-x)=x^2\]
Squaring multiplies the expression by itself. Two negative factors give a positive product.

This pair illustrates the symbolic proof; it is not a substitute for that proof.

questions.prompt: For a function continuous at x = a, the limit as x approaches a equals what?
questions.explanation:
\[\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=f(a)\]
Continuity at a means the approached value exists and equals the function value at a. This equality is precisely the condition needed to substitute directly.

\[\frac{d}{dx}(3x)=3\frac{d}{dx}x\]
A constant multiplier stays outside the derivative.

\[\frac{d}{dx}x=1\]
The function x changes one unit for each unit increase of its input.

\[3\cdot1=3\]
Multiply the constant by the derivative.
